profile.campus: Alliance Gateway, Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Texas (Meta's Fort Worth data center campus, expanded to five buildings)
profile.address: 4500, Like Way, Alliance Gateway North, Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Texas, 76262
profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 1 of 3 mapped in this cluster, westernmost to easternmost ordering) is part of Meta's Fort Worth campus in the Alliance Gateway development in Tarrant County, Texas. Facebook broke ground in 2015 with an original plan for three buildings, expanded to five buildings in 2017, and reached more than 2.6 million square feet campus-wide, according to Data Center Dynamics; the campus is notable as a cold-storage facility built to hold posts, photos, and videos rarely accessed by users, one of only four such Facebook/Meta facilities operated worldwide at the time DCD reported on it. Facebook began construction on the final phase in December 2020, targeting completion in 2022, at a total campus investment of about $1.5 billion, including a $200 million addition specifically to expand cold-storage capacity; staffing was reported at over 150 employees during that final phase, rising toward about 200 staff (Meta employees and contractors) once complete. The campus is LEED Gold certified and reported as powered by 100% renewable energy sourced from roughly 200 megawatts of Texas wind power, with on-site diesel generators for backup, per DCD's reporting; a third-party aggregator listing (DataCenterMap, not an operator-confirmed source) separately cites a similar 200 MW figure for the site, which is treated here only as corroboration of the wind-power figure already reported by DCD, not as an independent primary source. Meta's own current fact sheet for the campus reports more than $1.5 billion invested, groundbreaking dated to 2015, roughly 200-plus operational jobs, 1,200 peak skilled-trade construction workers, more than $5.2 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, and participation in a Meta-supported program adding more than 9,000 megawatts of new renewable energy across more than 40 projects statewide in Texas, a regional grid contribution rather than a Fort Worth-specific figure. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact current building count, or per-building square footage for individual Fort Worth structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

profile.capacity_note: Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity or exact per-building square footage for Fort Worth; Data Center Dynamics reported the five-building campus at more than 2.6 million square feet total, applied here as a campus-wide figure rather than a per-building one. A third-party aggregator (DataCenterMap) figure of 200 MW is noted only as corroborating DCD's reported wind-power figure, not adopted as an independently confirmed capacity number.
profile.facility_note: One of three Meta buildings OpenStreetMap groups together at this Fort Worth location (the wider campus has five buildings per Data Center Dynamics; OSM maps three).

profile.regional_context: Fort Worth's Alliance Gateway area, near Fort Worth Alliance Airport, has grown into a broader data center corridor beyond Meta, per Fort Worth Report's coverage of the area's data center development; Meta's campus predates much of that later growth, having broken ground in 2015.

reading.body:
Meta owns a data center campus in Fort Worth, Tarrant County. No power capacity is published for this facility. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities overall, of which 18 publish megawatt figures totaling 468 MW. This campus does not appear in those 18 published figures, placing it outside the ranked capacity tier despite verified Meta ownership.

The research record for this site is exhausted. Location, address, and ownership are verified as of September 2026. Opening date, investment, building count, and power consumption are not published by Meta for this specific facility. Regional Wikipedia sources for Fort Worth and Tarrant County either omit the facility entirely or contain only generic Meta company-level information. Direct operator spec pages have not been consulted for detailed campus specifications.

Meta's data center program spans multiple facilities across the United States, including a separate 10 billion dollar AI data center project in northeast Louisiana announced in December 2024. Whether the Fort Worth campus will matter to AI scaling depends on published capacity figures that do not yet exist in accessible sources. Until Meta publishes specifications for this site, its role in the company's AI infrastructure and the state's overall compute capacity remains unknown.
